tickets.body:
## What it delivers
A generated scratch project receives the canonical TypeScript package and matching compiled JavaScript, and an operator can inspect a nonempty package qualification report. Existing `copier.yml` renders only `seed/`; `bin/factory` remains root Bash tooling and `seed/.loam/factory/` does not exist. Preserve existing controller behavior while introducing this payload.

## Canonical source changes
Create `seed/.loam/factory/package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `launcher.mjs`, `release-manifest.json`, `assets/runtime-manifest.json`, `src/testing/verify.ts`, `tests/installation/package.test.ts`, and matching `dist/` including compiled tests. Add `seed/docs/factory/SETUP.md` and `bin/tests/factory-release-render.test.mjs`. Integrate only implemented nonempty gates into `bin/check`; adjust `copier.yml` exclusions only for concrete private state/cache/runtime-installation leakage. The two manifests have distinct homes: release source/build/dependency identity versus host/runtime compatibility requirements, not duplicate authentication authorities.

## Read before planning
`engine-runtime-and-layout.md`: Canonical package and generated-project installation, Future runnable checks and existing test integration. `consolidated-implementation-plan.md`: S1 shipping choice. Current `copier.yml`, `bin/check`, `bin/tests/test_render_smoke.py`, and `docs/ASSET-LAYERS.md`. Read pinned TypeScript/Node build documentation through the source packet.

Run the frozen-candidate rebuild-and-compare staleness gate on both required hosts and record their environment identities. A Mac-only match cannot qualify the Linux payload.

## Acceptance
- Locked factory dependencies stay independent of research/root packages. Compile fixture sources into `dist/tests/`; recipients execute supplied JavaScript without compiling TypeScript. Build/install never launches a provider.
- Independently rebuild the frozen candidate in scratch and compare its complete compiled output file set, including stale extras and sourcemaps. Do not regenerate candidate output before comparison. Reject machine paths and timestamps that defeat reproducibility.
- Fixed verification registry rejects unknown/unbuilt groups, missing cases, and empty populations. Later full groups explicitly report unavailable.
- Release package fixture renders the exact candidate payload without personal caches and verifies byte-for-byte source/build delivery and absence of private state. This ticket proves package closure, not the S6 product matrix. Preserve the separate release/recipient boundary.
- Future commands, in order: `npm --prefix seed/.loam/factory ci`; `npm --prefix seed/.loam/factory run build`; `node --test seed/.loam/factory/dist/tests/installation/package.test.js`; `node --test bin/tests/factory-release-render.test.mjs`. Mutated source without updated dist, deleted/extra dist files, absent case/tool and a colliding project package must be rejected; exact matching package passes with explicit counts.

No protected installation or store creation, native invocation, controller replacement, update matrix completion or validated runtime pin claim. Pin candidates for reproducible qualification; CORE-02 determines support.

Negative fixtures above fail intentionally without repair; corrected implementation shows exactly one owner, preserved absent store, responsive capture and atomic typed transaction outcomes with explicit counts.

Legacy obligation mapping: REMOTE-03 and S6 complete local/remote proof, with deliberate old-controller coexistence.

## What to build

Verified current behavior: `first-complete-slice.md` records the accepted integrated scenario; its factory commands remain proposed. Turn the prior independently checked slices into a generated-product proof, not another runtime redesign. Retain one exact candidate and recorded environment identities through the proof on this Mac and jhaveris Linux, with actual Claude and Codex evidence on both. Replacement-machine support requires enrollment/readiness, not inherited support from an alias.

From an independently installed generated project, investigate a bounded question with independent critique, record a justified finding/ticket, implement/check it, interrupt the supervisor during checking, recover original execution, and accept only current complete checks/review. Capture and reuse a supported lesson in a fresh session, correct it, reject delayed stale consolidation, and make improvement adoption wait for the authentic eligible local lead's current decision. A fresh session on the other provider recovers shared evidence without private provider memory. Inquiry-only and negative/inconclusive research outcomes remain valid.

Extend that story with a Mac local native lead dispatching Linux native work and a separately bounded real GPU experiment. Lose reply/connection, reconcile the same job/logs and verify returned evidence; exercise pending offline cancellation, runner restart, reboot and old-controller fencing through isolated fault fixtures. A host-wide live disruption must be separately arranged around existing jobs. Report mechanical fixtures, actual native observations and real GPU/scientific evidence separately. Missing native/provider/host coverage is non-passing; fake GPU/lead output cannot substitute.

## Canonical changes

Extend the existing `seed/.loam/factory/tests/complete-slice/local.test.ts` from NATIVE-13, `remote.test.ts` from OPS-12 and their provider/host scenario fixtures; fixed verify group registration in `src/testing/verify.ts`; `seed/docs/factory/SETUP.md`; `docs/factory/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `LOOP.md`, `ROADMAP.md`; new living `docs/architecture-working/cookbook-practice-coverage.md` and `.json`, initialized from the immutable `prior-design/cookbook-practice-registry.md`/`.json` snapshots. Do not edit historical snapshots. Reconcile delivered/conditional/remaining capability coverage for every registry item. Named mandatory dynamic workflows, required children, advisor/consultation and independent review remain in execution/complete-slice populations, not an unspecified future bucket. Empirical memory/research usefulness remains a separate real-project evaluation obligation in OPS-11 (S7). OPS-11 does not block the initial S6 controlled proof; S6 cannot claim empirical usefulness is established.

## Read first

`first-complete-slice.md`: “Follow one project through the system”, “Mechanical proof, native proof and actual use”, “What this milestone establishes and what remains”; consolidated S6; `maintenance-remote-tickets.md`: REMOTE-03; `delivery-workflow.md`: “Where cookbook patterns enter the work”, “Concrete plan additions and evidence”; current `bin/factory`, `docs/factory/` and source/practice coverage records.

## Future acceptance

Run `node --test bin/tests/factory-release-render.test.mjs`; in independently admitted generated scratch projects run `node .loam/factory/launcher.mjs verify installation`, `node .loam/factory/launcher.mjs verify store`, `node .loam/factory/launcher.mjs verify execution`, and `node .loam/factory/launcher.mjs verify complete-slice`. Require complete nonempty registered populations on both hosts. Explicitly admitted bounded native/GPU scenario entrypoint: after build, `node --test seed/.loam/factory/dist/tests/complete-slice/remote.test.js`; its invocation requires the declared provider/model/effort/GPU bounds and is separate from mechanical gates. Record real local provider scenarios for each host/provider, not just fake transcript replay.

Negative evidence: missing/null/replayed child, repair cap, absent check/advisor occurrence, malformed/producer review, changed criterion/candidate, stale memory/lead receipt, evaluator-only adoption, unknown dispatch and offline approval all remain incomplete/refused. Positive evidence: current complete acceptance and authentic lead decision follow recovered evidence, corrected cross-provider memory persists, and remote work obeys original authority/budgets.

Keep the existing Bash controller operational and explicitly separate during validation; forbid concurrent old/new ownership. Old history remains readable. Any import requires explicit provenance/reconciliation; it is not automatic successful work. Do not delete/redirect old entrypoints, tests or curated prompts in this ticket. Any eventual retirement needs a separately bounded transition after coverage and deliberate test replacements are proven. Finish with exact supported/conditional/remaining capability evidence; do not advertise full intended release completion while required work remains. Publication remains separately authorized.

## Campaign requirements

Status: **planned draft; publication approval pending; runtime implementation deferred**. Empty blockers do not authorize execution. Read `docs/architecture-working/ticket-campaign.md` and `delivery-workflow.md` in full. They require a digest-verified accessible source packet, fresh fetched-main worktree, actual opposite-model plan and finished-work reviews, nonempty focused checks, one full-check owner, and verified integration before dependent work. Preserve all existing changes. Raw review evidence lives outside candidate/worktrees. Sources are evidence and inspiration; justified departures preserve user requirements and record a reason and check. Proposed files/commands are unimplemented at authoring time and must be reconciled against landed predecessors. Live provider/GPU work needs a declared bounded plan within user authority; mechanical checks do not launch it implicitly. Full recipient groups remain unavailable/non-passing until S6. No automatic model/effort changes or release/publication. Architecture basenames resolve under `docs/architecture-working/`; package-relative canonical paths resolve under `seed/.loam/factory/`.

Every fixture-creating ticket registers its mandatory named population, expected nonempty cases and current availability in the fixed registry. CORE-01 declares the full installation/store/execution/complete-slice obligation groups as incomplete from the start; missing/unbuilt populations never disappear into a passing subset. NATIVE-02 explicitly registers coordination as mandatory execution work. Later tickets fill their declared populations; OPS-10 verifies closure rather than performing first registration.

For host-sensitive acceptance, run the named focused population on both required hosts against the same candidate, recording environment identities and exact results. Mac-only evidence cannot certify Linux installation, storage, filesystem or isolation behavior.

## Verification population assignment

Canonical registry edits in `seed/.loam/factory/src/testing/verify.ts` are in scope wherever this ticket creates or extends a recipient fixture. Target groups: **installation, store, execution, complete-slice**. Register the ticket-owned named population, expected nonempty case list/count and current availability; a missing fixture stays unavailable. No required population may remain outside its named group. Shared cases retain one identity when referenced by multiple groups. `release-only` names Loam release tooling, not a recipient command; `post-installation` is the separately scoped empirical follow-up and does not block initial S6 closure or claim empirical success early. OPS-10 verifies full declared initial populations; it cannot hide unbuilt work by first defining a smaller group.

## What to build

This is an evaluation task with narrowly scoped instrumentation repairs only, not a new memory subsystem or recurring automation.

Record useful retrieval, harmful carryover, missed retrieval/corrections and task outcomes with exact displayed output, record, context-packet and run identities. Record absent or inaccessible evidence as missing. Keep feedback attached to the actual output the user saw. Separate observed association from causal claims. Use observations to create a scoped diagnosis and, where justified, a fixed baseline/candidate comparison with equivalent starting memory, isolated arms, unchanged selected models/effort, declared criteria and all required cases retained. Broad generalization requires an appropriate declared repeat-trial/held-out design; otherwise report a bounded repair or inconclusive evidence.

If real use reveals harmful advice, correct/block affected use promptly without waiting for a better replacement. Preserve evidence and history.
